critical_code_review_comments: create_lock_policy_template returns default status 200 despite spec saying 201; FastAPI returns 200 because response_model overrides. If 201 is contractually required, set status_code=201 on the route decorator.
delete endpoint returns {'deleted': 0} with 200 when tpl_id doesn't exist (silent no-op). Consider returning 404 to match PATCH's behaviour for a consistent contract.

UserManagement.jsx grew further with template UI (now managing templates state + save + apply + delete); still ~1900 lines — extract UserLockPolicyModal into its own file (repeat of iter60/61/62 note).
Template `lock_flags` whitelist filter drops unknown keys silently (good), but no server-side warning is echoed — client sending typo'd keys will silently lose them.
PATCH accepts req.lock_flags is None to skip; but if client sends {} explicitly it clears all flags. Document this behaviour or reject empty dicts.
No cap on number of templates per user/globally — potential UX degradation if collection grows unbounded.
